name: chrome-devtools-mcp
one_liner: Gives an AI coding agent its own eyes inside a real Chrome browser, so it can click around, read console errors, and check performance itself instead of guessing.
buyer: A QA lead or dev agency running multiple AI coding agents who wants agents to catch broken buttons and console errors themselves before a human reviewer ever looks.
business_use_cases: A QA team wires it into CI so every pull request gets an agent-run browser trace and screenshot attached automatically.
A solo indie SaaS founder has their coding agent debug a slow page itself using real performance traces, skipping a freelance performance consultant.
An agency building client websites uses it to give its agents real eyes on rendering bugs across different client environments.

money_ideas.idea: A managed CI add-on that turns agent traces and screenshots into a shareable report for non-technical stakeholders

steal_this: Build a thin wrapper that posts agent-caught console errors and a screenshot straight into a client's Slack channel, and sell it to one small dev team this weekend.
